To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exercising for appearance versus health motives are associated with latent classes of poor mental health and well-being, which suggests that exercising for appearance may undermine mental health beyond its effects on body image and disorded eating.
Exercising to manage appearance may be associated with poorer mental health, and this relationship is not explained by body image or disordered eating.

(a) appearance motives for exercise predicted membership in a class characterized by elevated levels of depressive symptoms, anxiety, and psychological distress, and reduced levels of self compassion, life satisfaction, and flourishing, (b) health motives for exercise predicted lower odds of belonging to a class characterized by poor mental health and reduced well being, and (c) appearance motives for exercising predicted lower odds of membership in a well being class.
